_comment: Up to v0.9, zlint's `rules` block was an ALLOWLIST: naming ANY rule disabled every
rule not named, so a config listing only the rules you wanted off silently disabled
all the others and the tree reported '0 errors, 0 warnings' vacuously. v0.10.0 made
it an override layer (unnamed rules run at their defaults). This file still names
all seventeen, so what runs is a decision recorded here rather than a default that
arrives with a version bump, and the canary in scripts/check.py still has to fail.
OFF, deliberately -- each is a house convention rather than a latent bug:
suppressed-errors (29 hits): `catch {}` on best-effort cleanup paths, where the
only alternative is to fail a shutdown because a close() returned an error.
Each site carries a comment saying why the error is not actionable. Turning
this to `warn` would mean 29 permanent warnings nobody reads, which is worse
than an explicit decision recorded here.
unsafe-undefined (30 hits): `var x: T = undefined` immediately before the call
that fills it -- clock_gettime, read buffers, HPACK scratch. §6.3 forbids
allocation on the request path, so preallocated-then-filled is the house
pattern and it appears everywhere.
no-print (1 hit): bench/micro/main.zig prints its own measurements. A benchmark
whose purpose is emitting numbers is the one place std.debug.print is correct.
case-convention (7 hits, all in bench/isa/asm_probe.zig): `export fn sm_dot_f32`
and friends. §6.6.3 requires each kernel be a real symbol so objdump can find
it and docs/asm/ can be diffed; C-ABI exports are snake_case by convention and
Zig follows C for extern/export. Every hit is in that one file and every one is
deliberate.
duplicate-case (6 hits since v0.10.0): it now flags switch arms with identical
bodies, not duplicate values, which Zig already rejects at compile time. Every
hit is a protobuf decoder skipping a field (`3 => try r.skip(...)` beside `4 =>`)
where each arm says why its field is skipped; merging them loses that.
allocator-first-param (15 hits): strawmANN threads the *subject* first --
`searchQuantized(coll, query, ..., alloc, out)` -- so a call site reads as the
thing being operated on followed by how. Moving the allocator first would read
worse at 15 sites to satisfy a convention the codebase does not hold.
Everything else is ON. `unused-decls` in particular stays on because dead code is
how a tier ends up implemented, unit-tested and never wired into a run -- which is
what happened to T4 and to five of §8.6's seven metamorphic properties.
A clean run is therefore MEANINGFUL rather than vacuous: the canary test is to add
an unused decl and confirm zlint still fails.
